rationale:
Decision: split into five new children. Every child is a self-contained analytic lemma extracted from the supplied 12-step proof. The parent keeps only the glue around its two existing siblings, ted_lpm_curvature_holder and ted_lpm_fixed_cutoff_monotone. The split was machine-checked end to end (evidence below).

Why split. The supplied proof bundles five reusable obligations that use nothing about mu beyond their stated hypotheses:
(1) the C^1 cutoff family, step 4;
(2) the Hoelder-exponent algebra, step 3. It is used twice: in step 6 with cutoff weights and in step 9 with the indicator of B_t(y);
(3) dominated convergence for radial cutoff integrals, step 8. It is used twice: with g = 1 and with g = (x - y).H;
(4) the exponential perturbation bounds, step 11(a)-(d);
(5) the integrating-factor limit, steps 10-12: interval dominated convergence, the bound |int_0^r a_inf| <= (Lambda/4)(r/R)^alpha, and passing to the limit in Psi_k(s) <= Psi_k(r).

Separating them makes the proof safer:
- Together the five children are about 250 Lean lines and 29k heartbeats.
- What is left for the parent is about 240 lines and 65k heartbeats, instead of one roughly 500-line declaration.

A single-declaration leaf is also viable. The lp_monotonicity decomposition record reports a full single-theorem proof of this node within default heartbeats, and the aal analog was finally accepted as a single leaf. The split is preferred because the obligations are generic and separately reusable, the node budget is no longer binding, and every piece is already machine-checked.

This repeats a reviewed pattern:
- The analogous node aal_monotonicity_of_radial_identity (root.affine_approximation-a1.lp_monotonicity-a1.monotonicity_core-a1) proposed these same obligations as children (its aal_mrc_* split).
- That split passed three decomposition audits. It was never activated only because the node bound was then 200 (GMT/Scratch/aal_mrc/README.md).
- Today max_nodes = 1000 (swarm-project.json) and dag.json holds 411 nodes, so five new nodes fit.

No reuse is possible:
- No dag.json node, accepted or not, has any of the five types (whitespace-normalized string comparison over all 411 nodes).
- The now-accepted aal_monotonicity_of_radial_identity cannot replace this split. It needs a two-sided identity with a weight w, for every C^1 cutoff with T rho <= S. Hypothesis (A5) gives only an inequality, for antitone cutoffs with T rho < S.
- The aal_mrc_* lemmas were never DAG nodes.
- The allard52 branch has related but non-identical, non-accepted nodes: allard52_amcl_cutoff_sequence (implied by cutoff_sequence with delta = 1), allard52_amcl_radial_cutoff_tendsto and allard52_am_fc_a_bound. They cannot be reused, and this split does not solve any of them.
- The prefix ted_lpm_am_ occurs nowhere in dag.json, nodes/ or git history (git log --all -S).
- Dependencies are acyclic: integrating_factor_limit depends on exp_perturbation_bounds, and there are no other edges.

How the children and the existing siblings prove the selected statement. This is the parent's own remaining Lean work. Notation is that of the supplied proof: beta = n/p, alpha = 1 - beta, kappa = (p - n)/(4p) = alpha/4.

(P1) Steps 1-2.
- For t <= S, J(t) := int^-_{B_t(y)} |H|^p dmu <= J(S) < infinity, and t -> N(t) = J(t).toReal^(1/p) is nondecreasing on (-infinity, S]. Put K := N(R) >= 0 and KS := N(S) >= 0.
- Rewrite J(R) = ofReal(J(R).toReal) and apply ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff, Real.mul_rpow and Real.rpow_mul. The smallness hypothesis becomes K R^alpha <= kappa Lambda, hence K R^(1-beta)/(1-beta) <= Lambda/4.
- Also mu(B_t(y)) < infinity, H is integrable on B_t(y), and J(t) < infinity for every t <= S.

(P2) Step 4. Put delta := (S - R)/(2R) > 0 (the parent's eps_0), so that (1 + delta) R = (R + S)/2 < S.
- cutoff_sequence gives phi_k and eps_k with 0 < eps_k <= delta, each phi_k C^1, antitone and [0,1]-valued, phi_k = 1 on (-infinity, 1], phi_k = 0 on [1 + eps_k, infinity), and phi_k(s) eventually 0 for each s > 1.
- Hence phi_k = 0 on [1 + delta, infinity), and (1 + eps_k) R < S for every k.

(P3) Step 5. Put I_k(t) := int phi_k(r/t) dmu >= 0, L_k(t) := int phi_k(r/t)(x - y).H dmu and a_k(t) := L_k(t)/t^(n+1)/(1 + I_k(t)/t^n).

(P4) Step 6. Fix k and t > 0 with (1 + eps_k) t < S.
- Apply ted_lpm_curvature_holder with psi = phi_k(r/t), radius (1 + eps_k) t and p > 1. psi is continuous, [0,1]-valued, and 0 when r > (1 + eps_k) t.
- It gives |L_k(t)| <= (1 + eps_k) t N((1 + eps_k) t) I_k(t)^(1-1/p) <= t ((1 + delta) KS) I_k(t)^(1-1/p).
- coefficient_bound then gives |a_k(t)| <= M t^(-beta) with M := (1 + delta) KS. In particular this holds for t in (0, R].

(P5) Step 7. For each k apply ted_lpm_fixed_cutoff_monotone with phi_k, I_k, a_k, T := 1 + eps_k, S, M and beta.
- Its radial hypothesis is (A5) with phi_k, T = 1 + eps_k and rho.
- It yields ContinuousOn a_k on (0, S/(1 + eps_k)) and MonotoneOn Psi_k(rho) = exp(-int_0^rho a_k)(1 + I_k(rho)/rho^n) there.
- Since (1 + eps_k) R < S, (0, R] lies inside (0, S/(1 + eps_k)). So a_k is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, R] (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable), and Psi_k(s) <= Psi_k(r) whenever 0 < s <= r <= R.

(P6) Step 8.
- (x - y).H is integrable on B_S(y): it is bounded by S|H| there and is a.e.-strongly measurable via continuous_inner. The constant 1 is integrable on B_S(y) because mu(B_S(y)) < infinity.
- Fix t in (0, R]. Apply cutoff_integral_tendsto with T := 1 + delta >= 1 and (1 + delta) t <= (1 + delta) R < S, to g = 1 and to g = (x - y).H.
- This gives I_k(t) -> mu(B_t(y)).toReal (setIntegral_const) and L_k(t) -> int_{B_t(y)} (x - y).H dmu.
- Hence a_k(t) -> a_inf(t) (the parent's a_0) := (int_{B_t(y)} (x - y).H dmu)/t^(n+1)/(1 + mu(B_t(y)).toReal/t^n), because the denominator is >= 1.

(P7) Step 9. Fix t in (0, R].
- Apply ted_lpm_curvature_holder with psi = the indicator of B_t(y) and radius t. Rewrite its integrals with integral_indicator and setIntegral_const.
- It gives |L_inf(t)| <= t N(t) m(t)^(1-1/p) <= t K m(t)^(1-1/p), where L_inf(t) := int_{B_t(y)} (x - y).H dmu (the parent's L_0), m(t) := mu(B_t(y)).toReal and N(t) <= N(R) = K.
- coefficient_bound then gives |a_inf(t)| <= K t^(-beta).

(P8) Steps 10-12. Apply integrating_factor_limit with:
- R, beta = n/p < 1, M, K and Lambda, where (P1) supplies K R^(1-beta)/(1-beta) <= Lambda/4;
- a_k and a_inf, with (H1) and (H6) from (P5), (H2) from (P4), (H3) from (P6) and (H4) from (P7);
- Q_k(t) := 1 + I_k(t)/t^n and Q_inf(t) := 1 + mu(B_t(y)).toReal/t^n, with (H5) from (P6).

Take F(r) := exp(-int_0^r a_inf).
- Conclusion (i) of the child is the frozen (i) verbatim, since (r/R)^(1 - beta) = (r/R)^(1 - (n:R)/p).
- Conclusion (ii) of the child, F(s)Q_inf(s) <= F(r)Q_inf(r), is the frozen (ii), because F(t)Q_inf(t) = F(t)(mu(B_t(y)).toReal/t^n) + (F(t) - 1) + 1.

subproblems.title: C^1 cutoff sequence phi_k = 1 on (-infinity, 1], = 0 on [1 + eps_k, infinity), eps_k -> 0 (parent step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let delta > 0 be a real number (the Lean binder ε₁). Then there exist functions phi_k : R -> R and real numbers eps_k, indexed by k in N = {0, 1, 2, ...}, such that: (1) 0 < eps_k <= delta for every k; (2) eps_k -> 0 as k -> infinity; (3) every phi_k is C^1; (4) every phi_k is nonincreasing (antitone); (5) 0 <= phi_k(s) <= 1 for all k and all real s; (6) phi_k(s) = 1 for all k whenever s <= 1; (7) phi_k(s) = 0 whenever s >= 1 + eps_k; (8) for every real s > 1, phi_k(s) = 0 for all sufficiently large k.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ ε₁ : ℝ, 0 < ε₁ → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ k, 0 < ε k ∧ ε k ≤ ε₁) ∧ Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ (∀ k, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ k)) ∧ (∀ k, Antitone (φ k)) ∧ (∀ k s, 0 ≤ φ k s ∧ φ k s ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ k s, s ≤ 1 → φ k s = 1) ∧ (∀ k s, 1 + ε k ≤ s → φ k s = 0) ∧ (∀ s, 1 < s → ∀ᶠ k in atTop, φ k s = 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (cutoffs phi_k(u) = chi((u - 1)/e_k) with e_k = eps_0/(k + 1) and chi = 1 - Real.smoothTransition), with eps_0 renamed delta (Lean ε₁) and e_k renamed eps_k.

Let sigma := Real.smoothTransition (Mathlib). It is C^infinity, hence C^1 (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff); it is monotone (Real.smoothTransition.monotone); 0 <= sigma(x) <= 1 for all x (Real.smoothTransition.nonneg, Real.smoothTransition.le_one); sigma(x) = 0 for x <= 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos); and sigma(x) = 1 for x >= 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le). Define eps_k := delta/(k + 1) for k = 0, 1, 2, ... and phi_k(s) := 1 - sigma((s - 1)/eps_k).

1. Since delta > 0 and k + 1 >= 1 > 0, eps_k > 0; and eps_k = delta/(k + 1) <= delta because k + 1 >= 1 and delta >= 0. This is (1).
2. eps_k = delta * (1/(k + 1)) and 1/(k + 1) -> 0 as k -> infinity (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat), so eps_k -> delta * 0 = 0. This is (2).
3. The map s -> (s - 1)/eps_k is affine, hence C^1; composing with the C^1 function sigma and subtracting from the constant 1 gives that phi_k is C^1. This is (3).
4. If s <= t, then (s - 1)/eps_k <= (t - 1)/eps_k because eps_k > 0, so sigma((s - 1)/eps_k) <= sigma((t - 1)/eps_k) by monotonicity of sigma, i.e. phi_k(t) <= phi_k(s). This is (4).
5. From 0 <= sigma <= 1 we get 0 <= 1 - sigma((s - 1)/eps_k) <= 1. This is (5).
6. If s <= 1, then s - 1 <= 0 and eps_k > 0, so (s - 1)/eps_k <= 0, hence sigma((s - 1)/eps_k) = 0 and phi_k(s) = 1. This is (6).
7. If s >= 1 + eps_k, then s - 1 >= eps_k > 0, so (s - 1)/eps_k >= 1, hence sigma((s - 1)/eps_k) = 1 and phi_k(s) = 0. This is (7).
8. Let s > 1. Since s - 1 > 0 and eps_k -> 0 (item 2), there is k_0 such that eps_k <= s - 1 for all k >= k_0 (explicitly, any integer k_0 >= delta/(s - 1) works: for k >= k_0, k + 1 > delta/(s - 1), so eps_k = delta/(k + 1) < s - 1). For every such k, s >= 1 + eps_k, so phi_k(s) = 0 by item 7. This is (8).
proof_key_steps: Take eps_k := delta/(k + 1) and phi_k(s) := 1 - Real.smoothTransition((s - 1)/eps_k).
0 < eps_k <= delta and eps_k -> 0 since 1/(k + 1) -> 0.
phi_k is C^1, antitone and [0,1]-valued by the corresponding properties of smoothTransition and eps_k > 0.
phi_k(s) = 1 for s <= 1 (argument <= 0) and phi_k(s) = 0 for s >= 1 + eps_k (argument >= 1).
For s > 1, eventually eps_k <= s - 1, so phi_k(s) = 0 for all large k.

subproblems.title: Hoelder-coefficient algebra: |L| <= t K I^(1-1/p) implies |L/t^(n+1)/(1 + I/t^n)| <= K t^(-n/p) (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number and p, t, K, I, L real numbers with p > 1, t > 0, K >= 0 and I >= 0. If |L| <= t K I^(1 - 1/p) (real power), then |L / t^(n+1) / (1 + I/t^n)| <= K t^(-(n/p)) (real power), where t^(n+1) and t^n are natural-number powers.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (algebraic lemma) of the parent proof; beta = n/p there.

1. Exponent facts. From p > 1 we get p > 0 and 0 < 1/p < 1, hence 0 <= 1 - 1/p <= 1.
2. Put b := I/t^n. Since t^n > 0 and I >= 0, b >= 0 and I = b t^n.
3. Since b >= 0 and t^n > 0, I^(1-1/p) = (b t^n)^(1-1/p) = b^(1-1/p) (t^n)^(1-1/p) = b^(1-1/p) t^(n(1-1/p)) (Real.mul_rpow for nonnegative factors, Real.rpow_natCast, and Real.rpow_mul with t >= 0).
4. b^(1-1/p) <= 1 + b. If b <= 1, then b^(1-1/p) <= 1 <= 1 + b (Real.rpow_le_one, using 0 <= b <= 1 and exponent >= 0). If b >= 1, then b^(1-1/p) <= b^1 = b <= 1 + b (Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le, using b >= 1 and exponent <= 1).
5. Hence, since t K >= 0 and t^(n(1-1/p)) >= 0, |L| <= t K I^(1-1/p) = t K b^(1-1/p) t^(n(1-1/p)) <= t K (1 + b) t^(n(1-1/p)) = K (1 + b) (t * t^(n(1-1/p))).
6. Exponent identity. t * t^(n(1-1/p)) = t^(1 + n(1-1/p)) (Real.rpow_add with t > 0, t^1 = t), and 1 + n(1 - 1/p) = -(n/p) + (n + 1); so t * t^(n(1-1/p)) = t^(-(n/p)) * t^(n+1) (Real.rpow_add and Real.rpow_natCast).
7. Therefore |L| <= K t^(-(n/p)) (t^(n+1) (1 + b)). Since t^(n+1) > 0 and 1 + b >= 1 > 0, |L / t^(n+1) / (1 + b)| = |L| / (t^(n+1) (1 + b)) <= K t^(-(n/p)). As 1 + b = 1 + I/t^n, this is the claim.
proof_key_steps: b^(1-1/p) <= 1 + b because 0 <= 1 - 1/p <= 1 (cases b <= 1 and b >= 1).
Divide by t^(n+1)(1 + b) > 0.

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence for radial cutoff integrals: integral phi_k(|x - y|/t) g dmu -> integral over B_t(y) of g (parent step 8)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, E = R^(n+l) (Amb n l), mu a measure on E, g : E -> R, y in E, phi_k : R -> R (k in N), and S, T, t real numbers with t > 0, T >= 1 and T t <= S. Assume: g is mu-integrable on the closed ball B_S(y); every phi_k is continuous; 0 <= phi_k(s) <= 1 for all k and s; phi_k(s) = 1 for all k and all s <= 1; phi_k(s) = 0 for all k and all s >= T; and for every s > 1, phi_k(s) = 0 for all sufficiently large k. Then the Bochner integrals integral_E phi_k(|x - y|/t) g(x) dmu(x) converge, as k -> infinity, to the set integral of g over the closed ball B_t(y) with respect to mu.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (g : Amb n ℓ → ℝ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (φ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (S T t : ℝ), 0 < t → 1 ≤ T → T * t ≤ S → IntegrableOn g (closedBall y S) μ → (∀ k, Continuous (φ k)) → (∀ k s, 0 ≤ φ k s ∧ φ k s ≤ 1) → (∀ k s, s ≤ 1 → φ k s = 1) → (∀ k s, T ≤ s → φ k s = 0) → (∀ s, 1 < s → ∀ᶠ k in atTop, φ k s = 0) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, φ k (‖x - y‖ / t) * g x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in closedBall y t, g x ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof (restriction to B_S(y) and dominated convergence), written for a general integrand g; the parent applies it with g = 1 and g(x) = (x - y).H(x).

1. t <= S: since T >= 1 and t > 0, t = 1 * t <= T t <= S. Hence the closed ball B_t(y) is contained in B_S(y).
2. Let nu := mu restricted to B_S(y). Since g is mu-integrable on B_S(y), g is nu-integrable; in particular g is nu-a.e. strongly measurable and |g| is nu-integrable.
3. Vanishing off B_S(y). If x is not in B_S(y), then |x - y| > S >= T t, so |x - y|/t >= T (as t > 0), hence phi_k(|x - y|/t) = 0 and phi_k(|x - y|/t) g(x) = 0 for every k. Therefore, for every k, integral_E phi_k(|x - y|/t) g dmu = integral over B_S(y) of phi_k(|x - y|/t) g dmu = integral phi_k(|x - y|/t) g dnu (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
4. The limit value. Closed balls are measurable, so integral 1_{B_t(y)} g dnu = integral over B_t(y) of g d(nu) (integral_indicator) = integral over B_t(y) ∩ B_S(y) of g dmu (Measure.restrict_restrict), and B_t(y) ∩ B_S(y) = B_t(y) by item 1. So the claimed limit equals integral 1_{B_t(y)} g dnu.
5. Dominated convergence for nu (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence) with bound |g|:
 (a) each integrand x -> phi_k(|x - y|/t) g(x) is nu-a.e. strongly measurable, because phi_k composed with the continuous map x -> |x - y|/t is continuous and g is nu-a.e. strongly measurable;
 (b) |phi_k(|x - y|/t) g(x)| <= |g(x)| for every x and k, because 0 <= phi_k <= 1; and |g| is nu-integrable (item 2);
 (c) pointwise limit, for every x: if x is in B_t(y), then |x - y| <= t, so |x - y|/t <= 1, phi_k(|x - y|/t) = 1 for every k, and the sequence is constantly g(x) = 1_{B_t(y)}(x) g(x); if x is not in B_t(y), then |x - y| > t, so |x - y|/t > 1, hence phi_k(|x - y|/t) = 0 for all large k and the sequence is eventually 0 = 1_{B_t(y)}(x) g(x).
 Hence integral phi_k(|x - y|/t) g dnu -> integral 1_{B_t(y)} g dnu.
6. By items 3, 4 and 5, integral_E phi_k(|x - y|/t) g dmu -> integral over B_t(y) of g dmu.
proof_key_steps: t <= T t <= S, so B_t(y) is contained in B_S(y).
The integrand vanishes off B_S(y), so each mu-integral equals the integral for nu = mu restricted to B_S(y).
The target equals the nu-integral of 1_{B_t(y)} g.
Dominated convergence with bound |g|: the integrand is constantly g on B_t(y) and eventually 0 off B_t(y).

subproblems.title: Exponential bounds for a perturbation |u| <= (Lambda/4) q (parent step 11 (a)-(d))
subproblems.statement: Let Lambda, q, u be real numbers with Lambda > 0, 0 <= q <= 1 and |u| <= (Lambda/4) q. Then e^(-Lambda) <= e^u, e^u <= e^Lambda, |e^u - 1| <= (e^(Lambda/2)/2) Lambda q, and, if Lambda <= 1, |e^u - 1| <= Lambda q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Λ q u : ℝ), 0 < Λ → 0 ≤ q → q ≤ 1 → |u| ≤ Λ / 4 * q → Real.exp (-Λ) ≤ Real.exp u ∧ Real.exp u ≤ Real.exp Λ ∧ |Real.exp u - 1| ≤ Real.exp (Λ / 2) / 2 * Λ * q ∧ (Λ ≤ 1 → |Real.exp u - 1| ≤ Λ * q)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 11 (a)-(d) of the parent proof, with c renamed q and the parent's u = -integral_0^r a_0 (a_0 being the parent's limit coefficient) replaced by an arbitrary real u.

1. Put b := (Lambda/4) q. Then b >= 0 (Lambda > 0, q >= 0), b <= (Lambda/4) * 1 = Lambda/4 (q <= 1, Lambda/4 >= 0), and |u| <= b, i.e. -b <= u <= b.
2. (a) -Lambda <= -b <= u <= b <= Lambda/4 <= Lambda (b <= Lambda/4 and Lambda > 0), so by monotonicity of exp, e^(-Lambda) <= e^u <= e^Lambda.
3. Key estimate: |e^u - 1| <= e^b b.
 - Case u >= 0. Then e^u >= 1 + u >= 1 (Real.add_one_le_exp), so |e^u - 1| = e^u - 1. Also e^(-u) >= 1 - u (Real.add_one_le_exp at -u) and e^u e^(-u) = 1; multiplying e^(-u) >= 1 - u by e^u > 0 gives 1 >= (1 - u) e^u, i.e. e^u - 1 <= u e^u. Since 0 <= u <= b and 0 < e^u <= e^b, u e^u <= b e^b.
 - Case u <= 0. Then e^u <= 1, so |e^u - 1| = 1 - e^u, and e^u >= 1 + u gives 1 - e^u <= -u <= b. Since b >= 0 and e^b >= 1, b <= b e^b.
4. (b) Since b <= Lambda/4, e^b <= e^(Lambda/4), so by item 3 and b >= 0, |e^u - 1| <= e^(Lambda/4) b = (e^(Lambda/4)/4) (Lambda q). Moreover e^(Lambda/4) <= e^(Lambda/2) (Lambda/4 <= Lambda/2) and e^(Lambda/4) > 0, so e^(Lambda/4)/4 <= e^(Lambda/4)/2 <= e^(Lambda/2)/2. Multiplying by Lambda q >= 0 gives |e^u - 1| <= (e^(Lambda/2)/2) Lambda q.
5. (c) Assume Lambda <= 1. Then 0 < Lambda/4 <= 1/4, so |Lambda/4| <= 1 and Real.abs_exp_sub_one_le gives |e^(Lambda/4) - 1| <= 2 (Lambda/4) <= 1/2; hence e^(Lambda/4) <= 3/2 <= 4. By item 3 and e^b <= e^(Lambda/4): |e^u - 1| <= e^(Lambda/4) b <= 4 b = Lambda q.
proof_key_steps: b := (Lambda/4) q lies in [0, Lambda/4] and |u| <= b, which gives e^(-Lambda) <= e^u <= e^Lambda.
|e^u - 1| <= e^b b, from e^x >= 1 + x in the cases u >= 0 and u <= 0.
e^b b <= (e^(Lambda/4)/4) Lambda q <= (e^(Lambda/2)/2) Lambda q.
If Lambda <= 1, Real.abs_exp_sub_one_le gives e^(Lambda/4) <= 3/2 <= 4, so |e^u - 1| <= 4 b = Lambda q.

subproblems.title: Passage to the cutoff limit in the integrating-factor monotonicity, with the bounds on F (parent steps 10-12)
subproblems.statement: Let R, beta, M, K, Lambda be real numbers with R > 0, beta < 1, Lambda > 0 and K R^(1-beta)/(1 - beta) <= Lambda/4 (all powers with real exponents here, such as R^(1-beta), t^(-beta) and (r/R)^(1-beta), are real powers rpow). For k in N = {0, 1, 2, ...} let a_k, Q_k : R -> R. Separately, let a_inf, Q_inf : R -> R be the limit functions (the Lean variables a₀, Q₀; they are not the k = 0 terms). Assume: (H1) every a_k is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, R]; (H2) |a_k(t)| <= M t^(-beta) for every k and every t in (0, R]; (H3) a_k(t) -> a_inf(t) as k -> infinity for every t in (0, R]; (H4) |a_inf(t)| <= K t^(-beta) for every t in (0, R]; (H5) Q_k(t) -> Q_inf(t) for every t in (0, R]; (H6) for every k and all 0 < s <= r <= R, exp(-integral_0^s a_k(t) dt) Q_k(s) <= exp(-integral_0^r a_k(t) dt) Q_k(r) (interval integrals). Put F(r) := exp(-integral_0^r a_inf(t) dt). Then (i) for every r in (0, R]: e^(-Lambda) <= F(r), F(r) <= e^Lambda, |F(r) - 1| <= (e^(Lambda/2)/2) Lambda (r/R)^(1-beta), and, if Lambda <= 1, |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda (r/R)^(1-beta); and (ii) F(s) Q_inf(s) <= F(r) Q_inf(r) for all 0 < s <= r <= R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (R β M K Λ : ℝ) (a : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (a₀ : ℝ → ℝ) (Q : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (Q₀ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < R → β < 1 → 0 < Λ → K * R ^ (1 - β) / (1 - β) ≤ Λ / 4 → (∀ k, AEStronglyMeasurable (a k) (volume.restrict (Ioc 0 R))) → (∀ k t, 0 < t → t ≤ R → |a k t| ≤ M * t ^ (-β)) → (∀ t, 0 < t → t ≤ R → Tendsto (fun k => a k t) atTop (𝓝 (a₀ t))) → (∀ t, 0 < t → t ≤ R → |a₀ t| ≤ K * t ^ (-β)) → (∀ t, 0 < t → t ≤ R → Tendsto (fun k => Q k t) atTop (𝓝 (Q₀ t))) → (∀ k s r, 0 < s → s ≤ r → r ≤ R → Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..s, a k t) * Q k s ≤ Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..r, a k t) * Q k r) → (∀ r, 0 < r → r ≤ R → Real.exp (-Λ) ≤ Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..r, a₀ t) ∧ Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..r, a₀ t) ≤ Real.exp Λ ∧ |Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..r, a₀ t) - 1| ≤ Real.exp (Λ / 2) / 2 * Λ * (r / R) ^ (1 - β) ∧ (Λ ≤ 1 → |Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..r, a₀ t) - 1| ≤ Λ * (r / R) ^ (1 - β))) ∧ (∀ s r, 0 < s → s ≤ r → r ≤ R → Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..s, a₀ t) * Q₀ s ≤ Real.exp (-∫ t in (0)..r, a₀ t) * Q₀ r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 10, 11 and 12 of the parent proof (dominated convergence of integral_0^rho a_k, the bound |integral_0^r a_inf| <= (Lambda/4)(r/R)^alpha, the bounds (i), and passage to the limit in Psi_k(s) <= Psi_k(r)), stated for abstract sequences: beta plays the role of n/p (alpha = 1 - beta), M of (1 + eps_0) N_S, K of N_R, Q_k(t) of 1 + I_k(t)/t^n, and the limit functions a_inf and Q_inf play the roles of the parent's limit coefficient (written a_0 in the parent proof) and of 1 + m(t)/t^n. Step 4 uses the sibling ted_lpm_am_exp_perturbation_bounds: for real Lambda, q, u with Lambda > 0, 0 <= q <= 1 and |u| <= (Lambda/4) q, one has e^(-Lambda) <= e^u <= e^Lambda, |e^u - 1| <= (e^(Lambda/2)/2) Lambda q, and |e^u - 1| <= Lambda q if Lambda <= 1.

1. Integrable majorants. Since beta < 1, 1 - beta > 0 and -beta > -1. Hence for all real C and rho, t -> C t^(-beta) is interval integrable on [0, rho] (intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_rpow' for the exponent -beta > -1, multiplied by the constant C).
2. Convergence of the integrals. Fix rho in (0, R]. On (0, rho] (the interval uIoc 0 rho): (a) each a_k is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, rho], by (H1) and (0, rho] being a subset of (0, R] (restriction to a smaller set); (b) |a_k(t)| <= M t^(-beta) for every k and t in (0, rho], by (H2); (c) this majorant is interval integrable by item 1; (d) a_k(t) -> a_inf(t) for t in (0, rho], by (H3). By dominated convergence for interval integrals (intervalIntegral.tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), integral_0^rho a_k -> integral_0^rho a_inf.
3. Bound on integral_0^rho a_inf for rho in (0, R]. By (H4) and item 1, |integral_0^rho a_inf| <= integral_0^rho K t^(-beta) dt (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, as 0 <= rho). By integral_rpow (exponent -beta > -1) and 0^(1-beta) = 0, integral_0^rho K t^(-beta) dt = K rho^(1-beta)/(1 - beta). Since rho > 0 and R > 0, rho^(1-beta) = R^(1-beta) (rho/R)^(1-beta) (Real.div_rpow, R^(1-beta) > 0), so K rho^(1-beta)/(1 - beta) = [K R^(1-beta)/(1 - beta)] (rho/R)^(1-beta) <= (Lambda/4) (rho/R)^(1-beta), using the hypothesis K R^(1-beta)/(1 - beta) <= Lambda/4 and (rho/R)^(1-beta) >= 0. Thus |integral_0^rho a_inf| <= (Lambda/4) (rho/R)^(1-beta).
4. Proof of (i). Let r in (0, R] and q := (r/R)^(1-beta). Since 0 < r/R <= 1 and 1 - beta > 0, 0 <= q <= 1 (Real.rpow_nonneg, Real.rpow_le_one). Let u := -integral_0^r a_inf; then |u| = |integral_0^r a_inf| <= (Lambda/4) q by item 3, and F(r) = e^u. Applying ted_lpm_am_exp_perturbation_bounds to Lambda, q and u gives e^(-Lambda) <= F(r) <= e^Lambda, |F(r) - 1| <= (e^(Lambda/2)/2) Lambda (r/R)^(1-beta), and |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda (r/R)^(1-beta) when Lambda <= 1. This is (i).
5. Proof of (ii). Let 0 < s <= r <= R, so s and r lie in (0, R]. By item 2 (for rho = s and rho = r), negation and continuity of exp, exp(-integral_0^s a_k) -> F(s) and exp(-integral_0^r a_k) -> F(r). By (H5), Q_k(s) -> Q_inf(s) and Q_k(r) -> Q_inf(r). Products of convergent real sequences converge to the product of the limits, so exp(-integral_0^s a_k) Q_k(s) -> F(s) Q_inf(s) and exp(-integral_0^r a_k) Q_k(r) -> F(r) Q_inf(r). By (H6) the inequality exp(-integral_0^s a_k) Q_k(s) <= exp(-integral_0^r a_k) Q_k(r) holds for every k, and limits of real sequences preserve non-strict inequalities (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'). Hence F(s) Q_inf(s) <= F(r) Q_inf(r). This is (ii).
proof_key_steps: t -> C t^(-beta) is interval integrable on [0, rho] because -beta > -1.
Dominated convergence on (0, rho]: integral_0^rho a_k -> integral_0^rho a_inf for every rho in (0, R].
|integral_0^rho a_inf| <= K rho^(1-beta)/(1 - beta) = [K R^(1-beta)/(1 - beta)] (rho/R)^(1-beta) <= (Lambda/4)(rho/R)^(1-beta).
ted_lpm_am_exp_perturbation_bounds with q = (r/R)^(1-beta) and u = -integral_0^r a_inf gives (i).
Pass to the limit in (H6) using continuity of exp and (H5) to get (ii).
